SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE

COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Patient: Synthetic Patient (fictional), 58-year-old man
Date of service: November 9, 2026
Endoscopist: A. Current, MD (fictional)
Sedation: Monitored anesthesia care by the anesthesia team

Indication: Colorectal anastomotic stricture after a sigmoid colectomy in 2023; straining and narrow stools.

HISTORY
A colonoscopy in March 2024 found the anastomosis narrowed but passable. No dilation was carried out in 2024.

PROCEDURE
The colonoscope was advanced to the colorectal anastomosis at 20 cm, where a short benign-appearing stricture admitted the scope only with resistance. A through-the-scope balloon was passed across the stricture and inflated to 15 mm for 60 seconds. The colonoscope then passed easily and was advanced to the cecum; the appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve were identified.

IMPRESSION
Colorectal anastomotic stricture dilated with a through-the-scope balloon to 15 mm.
